description: Composite figure of five panels mixing one parameter plot, three electron micrographs and one mechanical-property plot. (a) plots W_R (×10⁻⁴ m; y-axis labelled 10–30) against Al content (wt.%, 0–6); three black data points at 0, 3 and 6 wt% Al (lying just below the 30 and 20 gridlines and on the 10 gridline) are joined by a descending straight line. Two grey circles with arrows mark the wavy-to-planar slip transition, labelled (a1) at about 1.5 wt% Al and (a2) at about 4.5 wt% Al. (a1) is an ECCI micrograph (200 nm scale bar, annotated "3Al ε=0.1") showing dark dislocation cells pointed to as "DCs". (a2) (200 nm scale bar, "6Al ε=0.1") shows dense parallel bands labelled "Planar slip". (b) is an ECCI/TEM micrograph (1 µm scale bar, ε = 0.14) of narrow, dense coplanar microbands. (c) plots true stress and strain hardening rate (MPa, 0–2500) versus true strain ε (0.0–0.5): a solid "Deformation until fracture" curve, a dotted "Strain hardening rate" curve, and straight dashed/dash-dotted lines annotated ε = 0.02, 0.05, 0.14, 0.27, 0.34; a grey marker with a downward arrow near ε≈0.14 links (c) to the microband micrograph (b). The group argues that rising Al content lowers W_R, switching slip from wavy to planar and producing microbands that sustain the work-hardening rate.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots W_R (×10⁻⁴ m) against Al content (wt.%) with three data points at 0, 3 and 6 wt% Al joined by a straight line of negative slope.
In panel (a) the three points lie just below the 30 and 20 gridlines and on the 10 gridline respectively, i.e. W_R falls monotonically as Al increases.
Two grey circles with arrows in panel (a) mark the transition from wavy slip (a1) to planar slip (a2) as a function of Al content.
Panel (a1) carries the annotations "200 nm" (scale bar) and "3Al ε=0.1" and shows dark cell structures pointed to by arrows labelled "DCs".
Panel (a2) carries the annotations "200 nm" (scale bar) and "6Al ε=0.1" and shows a white box labelled "Planar slip" with an arrow pointing to dense parallel slip bands.
Panel (b) is an ECCI micrograph with a 1 µm scale bar and the strain annotation ε = 0.14, showing narrow, dense coplanar microbands.
Panel (c) has a single y-axis labelled "True stress / Strain hardening rate (MPa)" spanning 0–2500 and an x-axis "True strain ε" spanning 0.0–0.5.
Panel (c) legend entries are: solid line "Deformation until fracture", dotted line "Strain hardening rate", and dash-dot/dashed lines annotated ε = 0.02, ε = 0.05, ε = 0.14, ε = 0.27, ε = 0.34.
A grey marker with a downward black arrow in panel (c) is placed near ε≈0.14 on the strain-hardening-rate curve, matching the ε = 0.14 strain of the microband micrograph in (b).
The caption states that the W_R evolution with Al content is used to predict the dislocation slipping transition from wavy (a1) to planar (a2) mode.
The caption states that panel (b) is a microstructure observation of microbands under ECCI.
The caption states that panel (c) gives the tensile and work hardening curves of Fe–Mn–C–Al steel with SRO effect, adapted with permission from refs [19,81] (Copyright 2018 and 2016, Elsevier).
The citing text states that the parameter W_R of Fe–22Mn–(0, 3, and 6) Al (wt%) low-density steel decreases with increasing Al content, supporting a stronger planar slipping mechanism.

The citing text describes Figure 6b as a TEM observation of SRO-induced coplanar slip bands and Figure 6c as the SRO effect on work hardening rate evolution, whereas the caption labels (b) as ECCI — the two descriptions of the (b) modality differ.

The citing text states that once SRO is destroyed, propagation of succeeding dislocations on the same glide plane is facilitated and microbands form with plastic strain, with accumulated dislocations causing long-range stress that contributes to work hardening.

subfigures.description: Scatter/line plot of W_R (×10⁻⁴ m) versus Al content (wt.%), with three black data points at 0, 3 and 6 wt% Al connected by a descending straight line, plus two grey circles with arrows labelling (a1) (about 1.5 wt% Al) and (a2) (about 4.5 wt% Al) as the wavy-to-planar slip transition.
Electron-channelling-contrast micrograph with a 200 nm scale bar, annotated "3Al ε=0.1"; two white arrows labelled "DCs" point to dark dislocation-cell structure typical of wavy slip.
Electron-channelling-contrast micrograph with a 200 nm scale bar, annotated "6Al ε=0.1"; a white box labelled "Planar slip" with an arrow points to dense parallel slip bands.
ECCI/TEM micrograph with a 1 µm scale bar and the annotation ε = 0.14, showing narrow, dense, parallel coplanar microbands running diagonally through the field.

True stress / strain hardening rate (MPa, 0–2500) versus true strain ε (0.0–0.5): solid curve "Deformation until fracture", dotted curve "Strain hardening rate", and straight dashed lines annotated ε = 0.02, 0.05, 0.14, 0.27, 0.34; a grey marker with a downward arrow sits near ε≈0.14.

unreadable_items: panel (c): the geometric construction and exact slope of the straight dashed lines annotated ε = 0.02, 0.05, 0.14, 0.27, 0.34 are not legible at the supplied resolution
panel (a): exact numeric values of the three W_R data points are not printed as labels; only gridline positions can be read
panel (b): no phase/feature annotation or crystallographic index is printed on the micrograph, so the microband character is read from morphology only
